long_biography.plain_text:
After Athens hosted the Olympic Games, Minos Kyriakou took the presidency of the Hellenic Olympic Committee. The appointment capped years of direct involvement in Greek athletics. He had led Panellinios Athletic Club, revived the Tsiklitiria meeting and helped raise it to the international Super Grand Prix calendar. He also completed a four-year term on the world athletics federation's council.

Kyriakou held the Olympic committee post for five years and also led the International Olympic Academy. These were not honorary attachments to his business career but a sustained administrative programme built around clubs, events and national institutions. When he died of a heart attack in July 2017, the Greek Olympic movement lowered flags at its offices, the Panathenaic Stadium and Olympia in recognition of that work.
